experiment: joint multi-piece re-placement (mode 29) as the third repair tier of the mode-26 clamped ladder: a clean negative on the multi-millimetre residue class

mechanism.ejection: every piece of every pair-bearing violation component (tier two ejects a vertex cover of the same graph), admitted by the shared local-repair limits micro_legalization_component_limit / replacement_ejection_limit
mechanism.orderSearch: every permutation of the ejection set up to 4 pieces (24 orders, lexicographic, identity first); rotations of the canonical descending-area order above that, capped at 24
mechanism.candidateStream: per piece: vacated pose, single-piece separating-projection trajectory, aimed displacement cloud, up to 3 nearest peers' vacated poses, skyline stations
mechanism.swapSeeding: one round; for each unordered pair the two vacated poses are exchanged in the anchor so each piece's whole cloud re-centres on the other's pocket; orientations stay with their own pieces
mechanism.budgets: one shared RunWork ledger for the whole pass; worst case 24 orders + 24 swap attempts, each over an ejection-limited set, funded by the existing per-piece construction quota terms (asserted in bounded_reinsertion_fits_the_construction_budget)

finding: the failure is not order-dependence and not the missing coordinated exchange - no order re-places even the pieces it already vacated (best 1/2, 3/4, 5/6). At these depths the vacated space of the whole component is already smaller than the component, so the residue is over-compression rather than mis-arrangement, exactly as the anchor-local characterization predicted.
remainingLever: the pass ejects every pair-bearing component in one set, so four independent 2-piece conflicts refuse on a cap (7) that none of them individually trips; 27 of 63 refusals are that cap. Per-component sequential repair would admit those.
